items.title: Nvidia Fallout, Microsoft Outage and Anthropic’s IPO Push
items.title_ko: Nvidia Fallout, Microsoft Outage and Anthropic’s IPO Push
items.summary_ko: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down the fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia as more details are revealed. Plus, Microsoft races to restore services after a global outage impacted government offices, traders and businesses worldwide; and Anthropic takes its IPO pitch to Wall Street as CEO Dario Amodei sits down with JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon.

items.title: Cerebras CEO: AI Infrastructure Opportunity Is Expanding
items.title_ko: Cerebras CEO: AI Infrastructure Opportunity Is Expanding
items.summary_ko: Cerebras is raising its outlook after third-quarter revenue jumped 55%, fueled by cloud and services sales that more than tripled. CEO Andrew Feldman discusses growing demand and pricing power for fast AI inference, new hyperscaler relationships with Microsoft, AWS and Oracle, and what Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation could mean for the competitive landscape.

items.title: Best Thing to Happen for China is Jensen Out of the Picture, Says Ives
items.title_ko: Best Thing to Happen for China is Jensen Out of the Picture, Says Ives
items.summary_ko: The fall of Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang has removed the industry’s most prominent opponent of US chip controls, setting up a showdown over potential new curbs that could accelerate China’s drive for semiconductor self-sufficiency.

items.title: Lutnick Under Pressure as Nvidia Crisis Unfolds
items.title_ko: Lutnick Under Pressure as Nvidia Crisis Unfolds
items.summary_ko: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is confronting accusations that his department didn’t do enough to keep Nvidia’s prized artificial intelligence chips out of China’s hands following Jensen Huang’s ouster as the company’s chief executive officer. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed Lutnick Friday for failing to blacklist a Singapore-based company, Megaspeed, over possible violations.
